expectations.text: Identifies that `make build` runs `go build ./...` which writes no binary
expectations.evidence: make build runs go build -p N ./... Passing ./... tells the Go toolchain to build every package, which it type-checks and discards. No output binary is written.

expectations.text: States that ./nexus3 in the repo root is therefore stale
expectations.evidence: The ./nexus3 file sitting in the repo root is a leftover from some previous explicit build and can be arbitrarily old.

expectations.text: Mentions the atomic-rename install because a plain cp hits 'Text file busy'
expectations.evidence: Then install with an atomic rename to avoid 'Text file busy' on any running supervisor that has the old binary open: cp nexus3 ~/.local/bin/nexus3.new && mv -f ~/.local/bin/nexus3.new ~/.local/bin/nexus3

expectations.text: Does NOT send the user back to re-read the flag parser
expectations.evidence: The case statement you've been re-reading is almost certainly fine. — explicitly reassures the parser is correct, directs fix at the binary not the code.
